name: Buick 231 V6, odd-fire (1975 to early 1977)
summary: 90-degree V6 on a three-throw crank with shared pins 120 degrees apart, so it fires at alternating 150 and 90 degree intervals: a syncopated lope at idle.

bank_angle_deg.note: 1975 Buick Chassis Service Manual, General Specifications: 'ENGINE TYPE 90 deg V-6'.

rod_length_mm.note: Not in the factory manual's specification pages that were read (only bearing length and clearances are given).

firing_order.note: Factory manual: cylinder numbers front to rear, left bank 1-3-5, right bank 2-4-6; left bank set slightly forward so opposite rods share a crankpin.

crank.value: three throws 120 degrees apart, each crank pin shared by the opposing pair (1-2, 3-4, 5-6); no split or offset pins
crank.note: Factory manual confirms opposite rods connect to the same crankpin. Wikipedia: 'three crank pins set at 120 deg apart, with opposing cylinders (1-2, 3-4, and 5-6) sharing a crank pin'.

firing_intervals_deg.note: Interval after each cylinder in firing order 1-6-5-4-3-2, i.e. 1 to 6 = 150, 6 to 5 = 90, 5 to 4 = 150, 4 to 3 = 90, 3 to 2 = 150, 2 to 1 = 90. Read from the article's step table (1 fires at 90, 6 at 240, 5 at 330, 4 at 480, 3 at 570, 2 at 720 crank degrees). The 150/90 alternation is also stated by Ate Up With Motor and Wikipedia's V6 engine page. Rule: 90 degrees between the two cylinders on one pin, 150 between pins.

intake_lift_mm.note: Not found in the pages read.

exhaust_lift_mm.note: Not found in the pages read.

peak_power_kw.note: 110 hp SAE net for the 1975 engine; rpm not given. Wikipedia says 105 or 110 hp depending on fitment and year.

peak_torque_nm.note: 175 lb-ft SAE net; rpm not given.

intake_type.value: plenum; cast-iron manifold with Rochester 2-barrel carburetor

header_type.value: cast-iron log manifolds, one per bank, joined by a crossover pipe
header_type.note: Manual removal procedure refers to right and left exhaust manifolds and 'exhaust crossover pipe'. Single exhaust with catalytic converter per Ate Up With Motor.

sources.what: 1975 Buick Chassis Service Manual, section 6A (engine), hosted by TeamBuick. Factory document: bore/stroke, CR, numbering, firing order, valve head diameters, rocker ratio.
jeepster-commando.com 'Understanding the odd-fire V6'. Enthusiast article with a step-by-step crank-angle table for the 225/231 odd-fire; source of the interval sequence and pin positions.
Ate Up With Motor history of the Buick V6, with a bibliography. 150/90 intervals, 8.0:1, 110 hp / 175 lb-ft, even-fire arriving during 1977.
Casting-number compilation: 1975-76 231 listed as odd-fire, straight rod pin crank; 1977 listed in both odd-fire and even-fire rows.

curb_kg.note: Infobox for the 1975-1980 generation: 'Curb weight 2,800 lb (1,270 kg)'. Rounded, for the generation, not specific to 1975 or to a gearbox. No factory weight found (not in the 1975 chassis manual or brochure).

gear_count.note: 1975 Buick Chassis Service Manual Fig. 4B-51 'Axle Assembly Ratio Usage H-X-A': 'H | 231 | 4-SPEED MANUAL | 2.56 ... THM 350 | 2.56' (checked by me on the page image). Brochure: 'Four-speed manual transmission is standard on Skyhawk and available on no other Buick ... Turbo Hydra-matic automatic transmission available' (https://www.lov2xlr8.no/brochures/buick/bilder/75_9.jpg). Choosing the automatic is my assumption.

gears.note: Table 'Gear ratios: THM350, 250, 250C': '1 2.52:1, 2 1.52:1, 3 1.00:1'. The Buick manual gives no gear ratios.

final_drive.note: Fig. 4B-51, H series 231: standard ratio 2.56 with the four-speed manual and with the THM 350 (codes DB, limited slip EB).

tyre.note: 1975 Buick brochure, Skyhawk page: 'Tires Standard: steel-belted radial-ply blackwall BR78-13'; 'Wheel size 13 x 5.00'. Rear-wheel drive.

driven.note: English Wikipedia, 'Buick Skyhawk' (read 2026-11-17), infobox layout: FR layout (first generation, 1975-1980; later generations front-wheel drive).

sources.what: 1975 Buick Chassis Service Manual section 4-B (rear axle), TeamBuick scan: axle ratios by series, engine and transmission (Fig. 4B-51).
1975 Buick US sales brochure, Skyhawk specification page (lov2xlr8.no scan): tyres, wheel size, standard and optional gearboxes.
Wikipedia, Buick Skyhawk: 231 as the only engine, gearboxes, curb weight of the 1975-80 car.
